ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system \(xOy\), it is known that the chord of \(\odot D\) intersecting the \(y\)-axis has a length of 6, and the center of the circle is \(D(2, 4)\). What is the length of the shortest chord passing through point \(B(2, 3)\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the intersection points of circle $D$ with the y-axis be $E$ and $A$. Connect $DE$. Draw $DC \perp y$-axis at $C$,

$\because$ The chord length of circle $D$ intersecting with the y-axis is 6,

$\therefore$ $AE = 6$,

$\therefore$ $CE = 3$,

$\because$ $D(2, 4)$,

$\therefore$ $CD = 2$,

$\therefore$ $DE= \sqrt{CD^{2}+CE^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}+3^{2}}=\sqrt{13}$,

$\because$ $D(2, 4)$, $B(2, 3)$,

$\therefore$ $DB \parallel y$-axis,

$\therefore$ Among all the chords through point $B(2, 3)$, the shortest chord is perpendicular to $DB$,

Draw $MN \perp DB$intersecting circle $D$ at $M$ and $N$. Connect $DN$,

In $\triangle DBN$, $\angle DBN=90^\circ$, $DB=1$, $DN= \sqrt{13}$,

$\therefore$ $BN= \sqrt{DN^{2}-BD^{2}}=2\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore$ $MN=2BN= 4\sqrt{3}$,

Hence, among all the chords through point $B(2, 3)$, the shortest chord length is $\boxed{4\sqrt{3}}$.

点 D(2,4) 与 B(2,3) 竖直对齐，DB=1。任取一条过 B 的直线，它截圆所得弦长为 2√(r^2-d^2)，其中 d 是圆心 D 到该直线的距离。要使弦长最短，需要使 d 最大。所有过 B 的直线中，D 到直线的最大距离为 DB=1，当且仅当该直线垂直于 DB，即水平直线 y=3 时取得。因此最短弦长为 2√(13-1)=2√12=4√3。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the Cartesian coordinate system \(xOy\), it is known that the chord of \(\odot D\) intersecting the \(y\)-axis has a length of 6, and the center of the circle is \(D(2, 4)\). What is the length of the shortest chord passing through point \(B(2, 3)\)?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the intersection points of circle $D$ with the y-axis be $E$ and $A$. Connect $DE$. Draw $DC \perp y$-axis at $C$.

$\because$ the chord of circle $D$ intersecting the y-axis has length 6,

$\therefore$ $AE = 6$,

$\therefore$ $CE = 3$,

$\because$ $D(2, 4)$,

$\therefore$ $CD = 2$,

$\therefore$ $DE = \sqrt{CD^{2}+CE^{2}} = \sqrt{2^{2}+3^{2}} = \sqrt{13}$.

$\because$ $D(2, 4)$, $B(2, 3)$,

$\therefore$ $DB \parallel y$-axis,

$\therefore$ among all the chords through point $B(2, 3)$, the shortest chord is perpendicular to $DB$.

Draw $MN \perp DB$ intersecting circle $D$ at $M$ and $N$. Connect $DN$.

In $\triangle DBN$, $\angle DBN = 90^\circ$, $DB = 1$, $DN = \sqrt{13}$,

$\therefore$ $BN = \sqrt{DN^{2}-BD^{2}} = 2\sqrt{3}$,

$\therefore$ $MN = 2BN = 4\sqrt{3}$.

Hence, among all the chords through point $B(2, 3)$, the shortest chord length is $\boxed{4\sqrt{3}}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangular coordinate system xOy; a circle intersects the y-axis, and the y-axis forms a vertical chord inside the circle; the center of the circle D is located to the right of the y-axis, and point B is located directly below D and inside the circle. Reasoning: Suppose the chord length formed by the two intersection points of the circle and the y-axis is 6. From the center of the circle D, draw a perpendicular to the y-axis, with foot C. Because the perpendicular from the center of the circle to a chord bisects the chord, the half-chord length is 3. Also because D(2,4), the distance from D to the y-axis is DC=2. Therefore the radius r of the circle satisfies r^2=2^2+3^2=13, namely r=√13. Since D(2,4) and B(2,3) have the same x-coordinate, DB=1, and DB is vertical. Among all chords passing through the interior point B of the circle, the shortest chord should make the distance from the center of the circle to the chord the greatest; therefore this chord is perpendicular to DB. At this time the distance from the center of the circle to the chord is DB=1, and the half-chord length is √(r^2-DB^2)=√(13-1)=√12=2√3, so the length of the entire shortest chord is 2×2√3=4√3.
